findings.title: Cache is not re-checked after taking the write lock, so concurrent misses reload and can overwrite a good cache with nil
findings.body:
`GetWebAssets` checks the cache under `RLock`, releases it, then takes the exclusive `Lock` without checking `entryPointAssetsCache` again.

In production (`cfg.Env != setting.Dev`), N requests that arrive while the cache is empty (e.g. at startup) all pass the read check. Each then takes the write lock in turn and re-reads and re-decodes `assets-manifest.json`. That is a serialized thundering herd on every cold start.

The redundant reloads can also lose data. Goroutine A loads the manifest and stores a valid cache. Goroutine B, queued behind it, reloads anyway. If B's read fails (transient I/O error, file being replaced during a deploy), line 69 sets `entryPointAssetsCache = nil` and B returns an error. B has thrown away a valid cached value that A had just stored.

Fix: after acquiring `Lock`, check again (`if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil { return entryPointAssetsCache, nil }`). Also consider not overwriting the cache when `err != nil`. Alternatively use `sync.Once` or `singleflight` for the non-dev path.
